name: Loke & Son Thermal Underlayer
description:
A long-sleeve thermal base layer that has been a staple of Great Lakes working-class wardrobes for decades. The waffle-knit fabric traps air efficiently and the flat-lock seams mean it can be worn under anything without bunching. Loke & Son makes this in twelve colors but the most common are cream, navy, and a faded red that everyone calls 'brick.' The neckline is a simple scoop — not styled, just functional. The cuffs are long enough to tuck under work gloves.

This is the shirt your grandfather wore under his overalls. It's the shirt you wear under everything from October to April. Loke & Son has made this essentially unchanged for forty years, which is either a mark of perfection or a lack of imagination depending on who you ask. Either way, it works.
what_it_says: You grew up somewhere cold. You know what actually matters in a shirt versus what's just marketing.
worn_by: the Gray Zone residents layering for winter
anyone who works outside in the Great Lakes corridor
story_hooks: Loke & Son is one of the few remaining independent clothing manufacturers in the corridor — a corponation has made a buyout offer that the third-generation owner is struggling to refuse.
During a the Gray Zone winter crisis, a Tier 3 aid organization is distributing these by the crate — someone is skimming the stock before it reaches distribution.
A character's only memento of a deceased mentor is a brick-red Loke & Son thermal, still folded the way the mentor always folded clothes.

physical_description.visual_profile: A fitted, understated thermal base layer with a utilitarian silhouette that disappears under outer wear. The waffle-knit texture creates subtle depth across the torso. Scoop neckline sits close to the collarbone without embellishment. Long sleeves taper to functional cuffs designed for glove integration. Overall impression: honest, unpretentious, built for purpose over fashion.
physical_description.fit: Slim but not restrictive—contoured to the body without compression. Designed to layer beneath work clothes and heavier outerwear without bulk. Sleeve length extends to wrist bone for glove overlap. Torso length hits at hip for secure tucking.
physical_description.primary_material: Synthetic thermal blend with moisture-wicking properties. Waffle-knit construction for maximum air-trapping insulation. Flat-lock seams throughout to eliminate chafing and bunching.
physical_description.texture: Waffle-knit surface creates a gridded, tactile appearance—visible under close inspection but subtle from a distance. Soft to touch despite industrial construction. No pills or snag points.
physical_description.color_scheme: Most common: cream (off-white), navy blue, or faded brick-red (weathered crimson). The brick-red shows age gracefully with slight color loss around collar and cuffs from repeated washing. Clean, monochromatic appearance.
physical_description.closures: None—simple pullover design. No zippers, buttons, or snaps.
distinctive_features: Flat-lock seams running the full length of sleeves and torso to prevent seam rolling
Extended cuffs engineered to sit under work gloves without slipping
Scoop neckline unadorned and minimal for layering compatibility
Small woven label at lower left ribs bearing 'LOKE & SON' in simple sans-serif
Waffle-knit texture visible across entire garment
Reinforced shoulder seams for durability under heavy outerwear
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3—functional working-class. Affordable, durable, designed for industrial work across the GLMZ.
physical_description.cultural_context: The uniform of factory workers, construction crews, warehouse operators, and dock laborers. A generational staple—worn by fathers and grandfathers. Signals dependability, no-nonsense practicality, and connection to Great Lakes manufacturing heritage. Worn by people who work indoors in cold environments: climate-controlled factories, unheated storage, refrigerated logistics centers.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in and well-worn. Slight fading in high-friction areas (collar, cuffs, shoulder seams). No visible holes unless heavily used. Likely to have minor pilling at underarms after multiple seasons. The brick-red variant particularly shows age with color loss that gives it character rather than degradation.
